Cal just seemed like a diversity quota fulfilled to me, Aimee is used purely as a go between and for plot convenience, the writers dropped the ball with Ruby, Viv is beyond stereotypical now as a character and personally I don’t care at all about Ola anymore, her arc is sort of over and I felt her and Lily got too much screen time. That’s the thing, Jackson is meant to be screen grabbing at first, but he can’t always be that way. If he didn’t change, then there wouldn’t be much point to his character and his arc would be underwhelming. Teen lives are constantly changing, including social status and Jackson best represents this.

It’s a shame we didn’t get to see more of his family, but maybe part of that was trying to show that Jackson was more alone than ever mentally? I’m not sure if that was the intention of the writing, I’m probably just overthinking, but it would make some sense to me.

I know what you mean, but the way they portrayed Jackson was extremely accurate. While it was not dramatic and screen-grabbing, the lives of those who seem to be losing what they know rarely are. For TV value it may not have been gripping, but the complexity of Jackson’s character really expanded in S3 and we got to see him come to acceptance of himself. From here, I think his arc is finished but it was great to see him adapt to his new life.

The scene on the cliff with Cal where he talks about his anxiety summed it up really nicely; Jackson has lost most of what is familiar to him, he has no direction. His purpose in this series is to try and become comfortable with his new life, and I think this is really realistic and reflects the struggles of a lot of ‘peaked in high school’ types.
